title: The gömböc always rolls back upright, with no weight hidden inside

cover.alt: A silvery metal gömböc, a rounded shape with sharp curved edges and a label reading 'Gömböc 1825', inside a round glass display case.

body: A roly-poly toy rights itself because its weight is packed into its base. A **gömböc** does the same trick while being convex and equally dense all the way through: on a flat surface it has just **one stable and one unstable** point of balance, so wherever you put it down, it ends up the same way up. The mathematician Vladimir Arnold asked in 1995 whether such a shape could exist at all. In 2006 the Hungarian scientists Gábor Domokos and Péter Várkonyi proved that it can, first with a mathematical example and then with a physical one. The name is a diminutive of the Hungarian word for sphere.

left.label: Roly-poly toy
left.text: Rights itself because its centre of mass sits low. Its material is not the same density throughout.

right.label: Gömböc
right.text: Convex and the same density everywhere, yet it still has only one stable and one unstable resting position.

slides.heading: Impossible in two dimensions
slides.text: A flat convex curve always has at least four points where its curvature peaks or dips, so a 2D version can't exist. Most people expected solid shapes to need four balance points too. Mathematician Vladimir Arnold suspected that in 3D the number could be smaller.

slides.prompt: On their honeymoon, gömböc co-discoverer Gábor Domokos and his wife tested 2,000 pebbles on Rhodes. How many behaved like one?
slides.detail: The shape is extremely rare and delicate: change it even slightly and it stops working.

slides.alt: An Indian star tortoise with a high, domed shell patterned with yellow star shapes, walking on gravel.
slides.caption: The domed Indian star tortoise has a shell much like a gömböc and rolls right side up without relying much on its short legs. Flatter tortoises need long necks and legs to flip over.

slides.question: Why doesn't a ball with a hollow inside count as a gömböc?
slides.explanation: A gömböc must be convex and homogeneous. Allow a cavity inside and the body is no longer convex, which makes a self-righting shape easy to build.
